header:
Date: 2025-07-15
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Narang (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM); Aisha Khan (StratusBank CISO), Liam O'Connor (Security Engineer), Marco Reyes (IT Ops), Nina Park (Legal)
Recording: Yes
Meeting purpose: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture review, discuss trust center artifacts, controls mapping, encryption/KMS, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, data residency

Summary: High-level review of Redwood's SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture, discussion of Trust Center access and mapping to StratusBank control framework, questions on audit logs, encryption and KMS integration, RBAC and SAML/SSO flows, and data residency options (VPC/private deployment vs hosted). Action items assigned to send reports, controls mapping, and schedule KMS deep-dive.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood. Uh Priya and Samir are with me. Um the plan today is to walk through our SOC 2 / ISO posture, show where docs live, and answer any mapping questions. Aisha, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Aisha Khan: Yeah thanks, good to meet you all. We wanted to get a clearer picture on evidence, like are you Type II or Type I? What the scope is, and how we can map controls to our internal GRC, um, for our audits. Also we have questions on KMS and data residency for production traffic.
[00:24] Priya Narang: Great, quick note, Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II and an ISO 27001 certificate for the control plane. The reports are available via our Trust Center \u2014 I can send the link \u2014 and we have a controls mapping spreadsheet that aligns Redwood controls to common frameworks, including NIST 800-53 and ISO controls.
[00:37] Liam O'Connor: When you say control plane, does that include Dedicated and Private deployments or just the hosted API? We need to be precise for our scope.
[00:45] Priya Narang: Good question. The SOC 2 report covers Redwood hosted services \u2014 our public Redwood API and the managed dedicated offering when it's run in Redwood-managed infrastructure under the contract. For Private deployments where you run the control plane in your VPC or on-prem, the scope differs \u2014 Redwood provides the platform but the customer controls the environment. We document that in the bridging notes; I'll point you to the section in the Trust Center.
[01:05] Marco Reyes: So for Private, basically vendor provides the software, and we need to show evidence for OS/hypervisor patching, network config, things like that?
[01:12] Priya Narang: Exactly \u2014 for Private we include an on-boarding checklist and a controls split matrix. It calls out shared responsibilities: Redwood covers application-level controls, authentication flows when you use Redwood's control plane, and audit log schemas; you maintain infrastructure controls like patching, host hardening, and network ACLs.
[01:28] Nina Park: Are there redacted versions of the SOC 2 report we can give to our auditors? We have to hand something to our external audit team.
[01:33] Jordan Lee: Yes, we typically provide a SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA. We also have an executive summary that's less sensitive that we can share immediately. I'll send the NDA and the exec summary after the call.
[01:45] Aisha Khan: On the SOC 2 report, we need to see the period covered and the list of in-scope systems \u2014 are logs and key management in scope?
[01:53] Priya Narang: The period is included in the report header. Key management is in scope for Redwood-managed KMS usage \u2014 we use a cloud KMS for host keys; for customer-managed KMS in Private deployments or Dedicated BYOK, the control is shared. The report will show Redwood's controls around key access and rotation for our managed mode.
[02:10] Liam O'Connor: On that BYOK front \u2014 does Redwood support connecting to our KMS in AWS or Azure? Does it support HSM or on-prem HSM over network?
[02:18] Priya Narang: We support customer-managed KMS in major clouds (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) and we can integrate with HSMs via networked KMIP-compatible endpoints for Private deployments. We'll need to validate network connectivity and certs during the integration. We'll also share recommended key rotation cadence and IAM policies.
[02:34] Marco Reyes: And what about encryption in transit and at rest?
[02:37] Samir Patel: All traffic to the Redwood hosted API is TLS 1.2/1.3 by default; at-rest encryption uses cloud-provider encryption for managed services. For customer-managed storage (Private), encryption at rest is your responsibility but we document recommended settings.
[02:50] Aisha Khan: Audit logs \u2014 how granular are they, how long do you retain them, and can we ship them to our SIEM?
[02:56] Priya Narang: We emit audit logs for admin actions, model changes, deployment events, and API request metadata. Default retention on hosted is 90 days in the Console, longer retention is an add-on. You can export logs to a customer's S3/GCS via a push or we can stream to a SIEM via syslog/Splunk forwarder. We'll share the schema; note that payload contents are sanitized (PII removed) per our data classification.
[03:19] Liam O'Connor: Can you include full request payloads or is that intentionally redacted? In our environment we need full request tracing to reproduce incidents.
[03:26] Priya Narang: By default request payloads with customer data are redacted from central logs for security and privacy. For Dedicated/Private we can offer configurable logging where you can opt into full payload retention under contractual terms and with appropriate encryption controls. That's typically part of a dedicated contract.
[03:41] Aisha Khan: SSO \u2014 we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. Does Redwood support both?
[03:47] Jordan Lee: Yes, we support SAML SSO for Console access and SCIM for user provisioning. For API keys we can tie keys to RBAC via the Console so admin can rotate and revoke. In Private deployments, SSO can be fronted by the customer's IdP.
[03:59] Marco Reyes: How granular is RBAC? Can we scope keys to specific models, routes, and environments?
[04:04] Priya Narang: RBAC is resource-based \u2014 you can scope tokens to routes, model versions, and per-environment access. We also support token-scoped rate limits and per-token auditing; the Console shows token usage and owner. We'll include screenshots in the controls mapping doc.
[04:20] Nina Park: For legal review, we need to understand data residency \u2014 where does inference happen and is customer data leaving region?
[04:27] Priya Narang: In hosted mode, inference runs in the region you select; we currently support NA, EU, and APAC regions. We route requests to the configured region as long as the model variant is available there. For Dedicated deployments we can pin pools to specific regions or availability zones. For Private, data never leaves your VPC if you deploy on-prem or in a customer-managed cloud region. We'll send a topology diagram.
[04:46] Liam O'Connor: There was a mention earlier of KV cache and prefix caching \u2014 any risk that cached prefixes could leak between customers?
[04:54] Priya Narang: Good catch. Caching is tenant-isolated. Our KV cache is namespaced per-tenant and we don't share state across tenants. That's covered in the architecture appendix in the Trust Center; I'll link to that.
[05:06] Aisha Khan: For the controls mapping spreadsheet, can you show which SOC 2 controls map to our internal control IDs? We need to ingest that into our GRC tool.
[05:12] Priya Narang: Yes the spreadsheet has columns: Redwood control ID, SOC 2 control reference, ISO 27001 clause, and a notes column for evidence type and location (e.g., log export, config screenshot, procedure doc). We can export as CSV for your GRC ingestion.
[05:26] Jordan Lee: Quick interjection \u2014 our Trust Center URL is https://trust.redwood.ai, I'll include it in the follow-up email along with instructions to request the full report via NDA.
[05:36] Nina Park: Regarding the NDA, what standard terms are you using? We usually prefer a mutual NDA and need to confirm the data handling section.
[05:43] Jordan Lee: We can use a mutual NDA; we have a standard template that most customers accept but we're happy to review your redlines. I'll cc Legal on the email.
[05:51] Liam O'Connor: Regarding penetration testing and vulnerability management \u2014 do you do internal pen tests and do you share remediation timelines?
[05:58] Priya Narang: We run regular third-party pen tests and internal scans. The SOC 2 report includes high-level statements about our vulnerability program; we can provide a summary of recent pentests under NDA. For Dedicated customers we also offer an option for cooperative testing where we coordinate the schedule.
[06:13] Marco Reyes: For network segmentation in Dedicated \u2014 can we enforce private peering between our VPC and the Redwood pool?
[06:19] Priya Narang: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and private link options in major clouds. For on-prem/private we can do a VPN or direct connect, depending on bandwidth needs.
[06:27] Aisha Khan: Let's talk about incident response and notification. If there's a compromise, what's the SLA for notification and what info do you provide?
[06:35] Samir Patel: Our incident response playbook calls for initial customer notification within 24 hours of detection for incidents impacting availability or data confidentiality. We provide a timeline of events, affected systems, mitigations, and recommended customer actions. For higher tiers we can provide faster updates and a named incident liaison.
[06:51] Aisha Khan: Do you have data breach insurance or cyber liability coverage details?
[06:55] Jordan Lee: Yes we maintain cyber liability insurance; we can share coverage details under NDA.
[07:02] Liam O'Connor: Back on the integration specifics \u2014 for KMS, how do you handle key access in the service? Does Redwood ever hold plaintext keys?
[07:09] Priya Narang: No, Redwood never stores plaintext customer keys. We store key references and use KMS APIs to sign/decrypt as needed. For BYOK we rotate ephemeral wrapping keys and keep minimal privileges. The Trust Center has a KMS integration guide that outlines the flows.
[07:24] Marco Reyes: Is there support for periodic key rotation without downtime? We need to meet our 90-day rotation policy.
[07:30] Priya Narang: Yes, we support seamless rotation patterns via versioned keys and can orchestrate a rotation with rolling updates so it doesn't cause downtime. We'll include the recommended pattern in the KMS deep-dive doc.
[07:42] Jordan Lee: I want to surface one common ask \u2014 customers ask for exportable evidence for SOC attestation checks. We provide screenshots, logs, and procedural docs. The mapping spreadsheet will show where each piece of evidence lives.
[07:53] Nina Park: Can you provide example evidence IDs that map to SOC control IDs so our auditors can cross-reference?
[07:58] Priya Narang: Yes, the spreadsheet includes evidence IDs and document links (internal to Trust Center). For sensitive artifacts we do require NDA to access the raw documents.
[08:09] Aisha Khan: For machine learning models themselves, do you treat model parameters as sensitive? If someone uploads a private model in Private deployment \u2014 is that backed up, and how is that encrypted?
[08:19] Priya Narang: Model artifacts are treated as customer data. In hosted mode, models are stored in our managed model store and encrypted at rest. Backups are encrypted and access-controlled. For Private, the model store resides in your environment. We'll include the model artifact handling section in the controls doc.
[08:36] Liam O'Connor: A small nit \u2014 in your documentation sometimes I see references to \"Redwood Serve\" and \"Redwood Console\" \u2014 can you confirm product names for our docs? We need consistent naming for our audit.
[08:45] Jordan Lee: Sorry about that, we have \"Redwood API\" (hosted inference), \"Redwood Dedicated\" (reserved capacity), and \"Redwood Private\" (VPC/on-prem). The Console is the operations UI. We'll supply a glossary in the mapping sheet to avoid confusion.
[08:58] Marco Reyes: On the audit log schema \u2014 can you show an example event line? We need field names for our SIEM ingestion.
[09:04] Priya Narang: Sure, the schema includes timestamp, tenant_id, user_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, source_ip, region, and a result code. We'll paste a scrubbed example in the controls doc.
[09:18] Aisha Khan: Are there admin-only APIs and how are they protected?
[09:22] Priya Narang: Admin APIs require mTLS to access in our backend; access is role-gated and logged. We do key rotation for system credentials and rotate service certificates regularly.
[09:31] Liam O'Connor: What about S3/GCS storage encryption keys \u2014 do you bring your own key or is it provider-managed by Redwood?
[09:38] Priya Narang: For hosted we use provider-managed encryption; for Dedicated and Private you can provide CMKs (customer-managed keys) and we will integrate so that you retain control.
[09:47] Nina Park: From a legal standpoint, do you have subprocessors list and data processing addendum (DPA)?
[09:52] Jordan Lee: Yes, we maintain a subprocessors list and a DPA that covers data processing, retention, deletion, and breach obligations. We'll attach those in the follow-up.
[09:59] Marco Reyes: Any recommendations for us to reduce compliance burden if we start with hosted then move to Dedicated?
[10:05] Samir Patel: We recommend starting with hosted to prove integration, then transition to Dedicated for stricter controls. During the transition we provide a migration checklist and assistance to fill in the controls matrix for the change in scope. Priya will own the migration playbook.
[10:18] Aisha Khan: For the follow-up meeting I'd like to focus on KMS, RBAC scoping, and audit log retention SLA. Can we schedule a 60-minute deep-dive?
[10:26] Jordan Lee: Absolutely \u2014 we'll propose times.
[10:29] Jordan Lee: Ok quick recap \u2014 action items: Jordan to share exec summary + NDA, Priya to share Trust Center link and controls mapping, Marco to share KMS vendor details. We'll get a KMS deep-dive on the calendar. Anything else?
[10:43] Nina Park: Please include legal language around data processing in the DPA.
[10:47] Jordan Lee: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[10:50] Aisha Khan: Thanks, bye.
[10:52] End of recording.
